title: What Is Hidden Under the Hair

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If a man or woman has a sore on their head or chin, the priest is to examine the sore, and if it appears to be more than skin deep and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease on the head or chin." - Lev 13:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The head and the chin. These are the places covered by hair — where something can develop unseen, hidden beneath the surface even from the person carrying it.

That is an apt picture of the mind. So much of our real struggle happens where no one can see: the thoughts we would never speak, the imagined conversations, the resentment rehearsed while we smile, the fantasy we return to, the anxiety that runs beneath a calm exterior all day long.

Nobody examines that. Nobody can.

Except that God can, and does. You have searched me, LORD, and you know me, wrote David. You perceive my thoughts from afar (Ps 139:1-2). Nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight (Heb 4:13).

For a person hiding something, that is unsettling. For a person who longs to be whole, it is the best news imaginable — because it means our real condition, the one no one else can examine, is fully known to the One who can heal it.

Paul speaks of taking captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ (2 Cor 10:5). That is not a call to perfect mental control. It is a call to stop treating the hidden places as none of God's business.

Bring what is under the hair into the light.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What thought patterns run in you that nobody else knows about?
2. Do you treat your inner life as God's concern, or as private territory?
3. What would it mean to invite God into your thought life this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You already know what runs through my mind. I stop hiding it. Search my thoughts, cleanse what should not be there, and make my inner life honest before You. Amen.
